chain.title: Whittle a Bone Flute
chain.desc: Two sticks and a bone - the cheapest way into the mod. Hold it and right click to open the melody browser: 55 tunes ship with the mod, and you can drop your own .midi or .abc files in to add more. It never wears out, though keep the materials handy - the bagpipes later eat three of them.

chain.title: Stretch a Tiny Drum
chain.desc: Leather over a log with string. Percussion rather than melody, and the instrument you hand to a second player when a group wants to play the same tune together.

chain.title: Build a Lute
chain.desc: Planks, a stick and string. The plucked-string voice, and the one most of the folk tunes in the built-in list were arranged for.

chain.title: String a Vielle
chain.desc: A bowed fiddle built from logs instead of planks. It sustains notes where the lute plucks them, so slow pieces sound completely different on it.

chain.title: Bore Out a Didgeridoo
chain.desc: Three planks and a piece of lapis. A droning low-end voice - it carries a bass line under someone else's flute better than it carries a tune on its own.

chain.title: Sew Bagpipes from Three Flutes
chain.desc: The only instrument built out of other instruments - three flutes and five leather. Loud and continuous, so put it in the hands of whoever wants to be heard across a whole village. Craft the spare flutes first.

chain.title: Assemble a Piano
chain.desc: Three bones and three note blocks, so it costs redstone. The cleanest, most neutral voice in the set and the safest choice for a complicated MIDI you imported yourself.

chain.title: Bend a Copper Triangle
chain.desc: Six copper ingots. A bright metallic ping - almost pure accent, so it earns its place in a band rather than as a solo instrument.

chain.title: Braze a Trumpet
chain.desc: Iron and copper. A brass voice that cuts through everything else playing nearby, which is what you want for fanfares and marches.

chain.title: Hammer a Handpan
chain.desc: Three copper ingots and three copper blocks - about thirty copper all in, the most expensive instrument here. A soft resonant drum that holds pitch, so unlike the tiny drum it can carry a melody.

chain.title: Craft the Ender Bass
chain.desc: Two note blocks around an ender pearl. The deepest voice in the mod and the last one you will be able to make, since it waits on your first endermen.

notes: The mod registers exactly 11 items, all in the immersive_melodies:instruments tag, and every one is a single shaped craft from vanilla materials - there is no tech tree here. The only genuine recipe dependency in the whole jar is bagpipe = 3 flutes + 5 leather, which is why the flute is first and the bagpipe sits mid-chain. Everything else is ordered by material cost: bone/stick -> leather/planks/logs -> lapis -> note blocks (redstone) -> copper -> iron+copper -> 30 copper -> ender pearl. Mechanically all 11 instruments are identical: assets/immersive_melodies/sounds.json gives each one the same 8 sampled octaves (c1-c8), so they differ only in timbre - do NOT write quests implying one has more range or does more damage. 55 melodies ship as .midi files in data/immersive_melodies/melodies/ (counted from the jar), and the GUI lang keys (immersive_melodies.search / favorite / tracks / free_playing / keyboard / error.unknown_file_type) confirm players can search and favourite them, play freely on the keyboard, connect a real MIDI device (MidiListener), and upload their own .abc or .midi files if the server permits. The mod also has mixins for allays, parrots, pillagers, piglins and zombies plus a util/EntityEquiper class, so mobs turn up carrying and playing these instruments - that is ambience, not a drop, and there is no loot table or advancement in the jar granting an instrument. Three advancement files exist and only one is real: data/immersive_melodies/advancements/misc/instruments.json, a recipe-unlock trigger on picking up a copper ingot. No structures, no loot tables, no entities of its own.
